Create a private Python environment for BirdNET

Source: R/birdnet_env.R
pam_birdnet_setup.Rd

Builds a virtual environment (never touching the system Python) with a pinned Python version. Uses uv when it is installed (it downloads the requested Python itself); otherwise falls back to reticulate, which needs a matching Python already installed.

Usage

pam_birdnet_setup(
  component = c("inference", "training"),
  python_version = "3.11",
  packages = NULL,
  envdir = pam_birdnet_env_dir(component),
  recreate = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  uv = pam_find_uv()
)

Arguments

component

"inference" (the birdnet package, used by Stage 3) or "training" (BirdNET-Analyzer, used only by the standalone training tools, which are not part of the workflow).

python_version

Python version for the environment. Default "3.11", chosen as widely supported by TensorFlow; change it if a package install reports an unsupported version.

packages

pip requirements. Defaults to pam_birdnet_default_requirements()[[component]].

envdir

Environment folder. Defaults to pamflow's private location.

recreate

If TRUE, delete and rebuild an existing environment.

dry_run

If TRUE, only return the plan without creating anything.

uv

Path to the uv executable. Found automatically when uv is on PATH or in a standard install location; set it if you installed uv elsewhere.

Value

Invisibly, a list: envdir, python, python_version, packages.

Details

Installing TensorFlow downloads roughly a gigabyte, so this can take several minutes. Afterwards run pam_birdnet_doctor().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pam_birdnet_setup("inference", dry_run = TRUE)
pam_birdnet_setup("inference")
pam_birdnet_setup("training")
} # }
